answer: Rotating cipher handoff. Each identity gets a one-time puzzle whose solution is the key to a fresh cipher; solving it yields a next puzzle, forming a chain only that agent can continue. To join, the agent must present a solved instance from an existing member's chain, which that member can spend only once. Benefits accrue per chain link, not per address. An attacker must obtain and solve a distinct fresh chain from an established island of members for every identity, buying or compromising real members one at a time.
